AI.motivation: Multi-core quantum architectures address qubit scalability limitations in monolithic NISQ devices, but effective circuit scheduling to reduce makespan, increase core utilization, and hide communication latency behind computation remains largely unexplored.
AI.method: The authors first introduce a layered scheduling baseline (parallel gates within same layer, sequential layers), then propose a greedy scheduling strategy that schedules each gate as soon as all its dependencies and required resources are available, enabling fine-grained parallelism across cores.
AI.result: On real benchmarks, greedy scheduling achieves an average 40% reduction in makespan and improvement in core utilization compared to the layered baseline.
AI.conclusion: Intelligent circuit scheduling that exploits parallelism can greatly enhance the speed of circuit execution in multi-core quantum architectures.

title: A Versatile Analytical Model for Fast and Accurate Determination of Feedline-Coupled Resonators for Superconducting Qubit Readout
summary: Superconducting quantum chips commonly utilize quarter-wavelength (λ/4) transmission line resonators as readout circuits. An analytical model for the accurate determination of resonance frequencies and coupling Q-factors of feedline-coupled superconducting resonators is introduced. The model leverages four-port microwave network analysis, integrating boundary conditions and conformal mapping techniques to compute even- and odd-mode impedances in edge-coupled coplanar waveguide (CPW) structures. Its versatility allows application to both planar and 3-D heterogeneous architectures, making it a powerful tool for resonator design. To validate the model, a test chip with λ/4 resonators of varying geometries is fabricated and measured in a cryogenic environment. Comparisons with finite element method (FEM) simulations and experimental measurements confirm the model's accuracy, with resonance frequencies and coupling Q-factors aligning closely across configurations. This proposed model facilitates the design of superconducting resonators in readout circuits for more effective, scalable, and adaptable quantum computing architectures.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an analytical model using four-port microwave network analysis and conformal mapping to accurately determine resonance frequencies and coupling Q-factors of λ/4 superconducting resonators in feedline-coupled CPW structures, validated against FEM simulations and cryogenic measurements for both planar and 3-D heterogeneous architectures.
AI.motivation: To provide an accurate and versatile analytical model for designing superconducting resonators in readout circuits, enabling more effective, scalable, and adaptable quantum computing architectures without relying solely on computationally expensive full-wave simulations.
AI.method: Four-port microwave network analysis integrating boundary conditions and conformal mapping to compute even- and odd-mode impedances in edge-coupled CPW structures; applicable to both planar and 3-D heterogeneous architectures.
AI.result: Validation through comparisons with FEM simulations and cryogenic measurements on a test chip with varying λ/4 resonator geometries shows close agreement in resonance frequencies and coupling Q-factors across configurations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed analytical model accurately predicts resonator performance, facilitating the design of superconducting readout circuits for scalable quantum computing.

title: Robust Quantum Memory Advantage from Contextuality
summary: Quantum contextuality is widely recognized as an essential non-classical resource underlying quantum technology, yet illuminating the precise mechanisms through which it translates into unconditional computational advantages remains an ongoing challenge. We demonstrate an exponential, noise-resilient memory advantage for quantum finite automata arising from graph-theoretic approaches to contextuality. We define a promise problem on an exclusivity graph $G$ for which any classical deterministic automaton acts as a non-contextual hidden variable model requiring at least $N=χ(G)$ states, where $χ(G)$ is the graph's chromatic number. In contrast, by exploiting a structural phenomenon we term \textit{representational contextuality}, a QFA solves this task using a memory of dimension at most $d=ξ(G)+1$, where $ξ(G)$ is the graph's orthogonal rank. This separation scales exponentially ($d=\mathcal O(n)$ versus $N=2^{Ω(n)}$) for Boolean-orthogonality graphs. Crucially, this memory advantage maintains an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ threshold against both depolarizing and coherent noise.

AI.tldr: Quantum finite automata leveraging graph-theoretic contextuality achieve exponential memory advantage over classical automata, with robustness against noise.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum contextuality translates into unconditional computational advantages, particularly in memory-limited settings.
AI.method: Define a promise problem on an exclusivity graph G; classical deterministic automata require at least N = χ(G) states (chromatic number), while quantum finite automata (QFA) using representational contextuality require at most d = ξ(G) + 1 states (orthogonal rank). Use Boolean-orthogonality graphs to show exponential separation.
AI.result: Exponential memory separation: d = O(n) versus N = 2^{Ω(n)}. The quantum advantage persists with an O(1) noise threshold against both depolarizing and coherent noise.
AI.conclusion: Contextuality, through representational contextuality, provides a provable and noise-resilient exponential memory advantage for quantum finite automata over classical counterparts.

title: Configuration-based understanding of superradiant phase transitions in Dicke lattices
comment: 12 Pages, 4 Figures, 2 Tables, Comments are welcomed
summary: The emergence of multiple superradiant phases in Dicke lattice models has attracted considerable attention in the quantum optics community. However, a unified understanding of the origin of multistability and its relation to different superradiant phases is still lacking. Here, we develop a configuration-based understanding to classify the superradiant phases in Dicke lattices. We show that photon hopping naturally organizes the possible superradiant configurations according to the lattice symmetry, providing a unified interpretation of the nonequilibrium phase diagram and the emergence of multistability. For the dissipative four-site Dicke lattice, we obtain the complete phase diagram and identify the coexistence of up to four stable superradiant phases. The proposed classification is further extended to five- and six-site lattices. Moreover, we demonstrate that the same configuration-based understanding also applies to the closed Dicke lattice, where the ground state uniquely selects one of the allowed configurations. Finally, we show that different configurations may belong to either same or distinct nonequilibrium universality classes in the dissipative Dicke lattice, while they share the same equilibrium universality class in the closed Dicke lattice. Our results provide a unified picture for understanding equilibrium and nonequilibrium superradiant phase transitions in Dicke lattices.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a configuration-based classification to unify understanding of superradiant phases and multistability in Dicke lattices, analyzing phase diagrams for 4-, 5-, and 6-site systems and comparing equilibrium vs. nonequilibrium universality classes.
AI.motivation: A unified understanding of the origin of multistability and its relation to different superradiant phases in Dicke lattice models is still lacking.
AI.method: The authors develop a configuration-based understanding that classifies superradiant phases according to lattice symmetry, induced by photon hopping.
AI.result: Complete phase diagram for the dissipative four-site Dicke lattice shows coexistence of up to four stable superradiant phases. The classification extends to five- and six-site lattices. Different configurations may belong to same or distinct nonequilibrium universality classes, but share the same equilibrium universality class in the closed Dicke lattice.
AI.conclusion: The configuration-based approach provides a unified picture for understanding both equilibrium and nonequilibrium superradiant phase transitions in Dicke lattices.

title: Near-Perfect Single-Photon Source via Ultrastrong Coupling
summary: Deterministic single-photon sources are indispensable core devices for quantum information technology, yet high-performance implementation remains a long-standing bottleneck for linear optical quantum computing. We propose a feasible scheme for deterministic single-photon emission based on a $\triangle$-type three-level atom coupled to a single-mode cavity, driven by two classical external fields, which is adaptable to both strong and ultrastrong cavity-atom coupling regimes. Under continuous-wave driving, the system achieves excellent single-photon characteristics: the normalized equal-time second-order correlation function reaches $g^{(2)}(0)\sim10^{-6}$, with a photon indistinguishability of $98.73\%$ and a state purity of $99.95\%$ in the strong coupling regime, while the ultrastrong coupling regime further suppresses $G^{(2)}(0)\sim10^{-8}$, yielding an indistinguishability of $99.10\%$ and a purity of $99.99\%$. For pulsed driving in the ultrastrong coupling regime, the source realizes superior performance, with an emission efficiency, indistinguishability, and purity of $99.96\%$, $98.98\%$, and $99.99\%$ under resonant conditions, and $100\%$, $95.91\%$, and $99.93\%$ under detuned conditions, respectively. The near-ideal optical performance of the proposed scheme provides a viable route for constructing high-quality deterministic single-photon sources, which offers a promising solution to the limitations of conventional single-photon devices and facilitates the further development of quantum information science and fundamental quantum optical research.

AI.tldr: A deterministic single-photon source scheme using a Δ-type three-level atom in a cavity achieves near-ideal performance: g(2)(0) ~10⁻⁶–10⁻⁸, indistinguishability >98.7%, and purity >99.9% across strong and ultrastrong coupling regimes under both continuous-wave and pulsed driving.
AI.motivation: Deterministic single-photon sources are critical for quantum information technology, but high-performance implementation has remained a bottleneck for linear optical quantum computing.
AI.method: A Δ-type three-level atom coupled to a single-mode cavity, driven by two classical external fields, operating in both strong and ultrastrong cavity-atom coupling regimes under continuous-wave and pulsed driving conditions.
AI.result: Strong coupling: g(2)(0)~10⁻⁶, indistinguishability 98.73%, purity 99.95%. Ultrastrong coupling: G(2)(0)~10⁻⁸, indistinguishability 99.10%, purity 99.99%. Pulsed ultrastrong: efficiency 99.96%, indistinguishability 98.98%, purity 99.99% (resonant); 100%, 95.91%, 99.93% (detuned).
AI.conclusion: The near-ideal performance offers a viable route for high-quality deterministic single-photon sources, overcoming limitations of conventional devices and advancing quantum information science.

title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
summary: Adaptive Derivative-Assembled Problem-Tailored variational quantum eigensolvers (ADAPT-VQE) represent one of the most promising approaches for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices. However, their optimization is slow and may stall due to vanishing parameters and redundant operators in the ansatz. In this work, we propose a simple strategy of operator elimination that removes non-contributing operators from the pool once they are detected, enabling the optimization to continue progressing toward convergence. We examine two variants, with and without pool restoration after elimination, and find that the former converges more smoothly and faster than the latter and the standard ADAPT-VQE. To capture dynamical correlations between the active space and its environment, we combine ADAPT-VQE with our recently developed downfolding approach, the one-body downfolding framework (OBDF). In OBDF, the bare molecular Hamiltonian in the active space is replaced by a correlated effective Hamiltonian that incorporates dynamical correlation effects outside the active space. We benchmark our implementation on a linear \ce{H_6} chain, an \ce{H_6} lattice, an \ce{H_6} ring, and the \ce{N_2} molecule using the OpenFermion simulator. Our results show that operator elimination significantly reduces circuit depth and iteration count, and that OBDF-ADAPT-VQE yields energies closer to the full configuration interaction (FCI) reference than the standard approach within the same active space.

AI.tldr: ADAPT-VQE is improved via operator elimination (removing non-contributing operators) and combined with one-body downfolding (OBDF) to incorporate dynamical correlations. Eliminating operators reduces circuit depth and iterations, and OBDF-ADAPT-VQE yields energies closer to FCI than standard ADAPT-VQE, as benchmarked on H6 systems and N2.
AI.motivation: ADAPT-VQE optimization is slow and may stall due to vanishing parameters and redundant operators; the authors aim to accelerate convergence and improve accuracy by eliminating non-contributing operators and incorporating dynamical correlations via downfolding.
AI.method: (1) Operator elimination: remove non-contributing operators from the pool once detected, with two variants (with/without pool restoration). (2) Combine ADAPT-VQE with one-body downfolding (OBDF) to construct a correlated effective Hamiltonian capturing dynamical correlations outside the active space. Benchmarked on linear H6, H6 lattice, H6 ring, and N2 using OpenFermion.
AI.result: Operator elimination reduces circuit depth and iteration count. Pool restoration (elimination with restoration) converges more smoothly and faster than elimination without restoration and standard ADAPT-VQE. OBDF-ADAPT-VQE yields energies closer to FCI reference than standard ADAPT-VQE within the same active space.
AI.conclusion: Operator elimination and OBDF integration significantly improve ADAPT-VQE efficiency and accuracy, offering a practical path toward better quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum devices.

title: Open Quantum Systems Driven by Chirped Pulses: Quantized versus Semiclassical Fields and the Validity of the Rotating-Wave Approximation
summary: Population transfer via chirped rapid adiabatic passage is studied using open quantum and semiclassical models, with and without the rotating-wave approximation. A time-dependent variational approach based on the multiple-Davydov D$_2$ trial state is employed to simulate the quantum models with an arbitrary finite mean photon number. We examine the accuracy of both the semiclassical field description and the rotating-wave approximation. Robust population transfer is identified over a wide parameter regime controlled by the laser spectral chirp and is found to be insensitive to the spin--phonon coupling strength, Gaussian pulse area, and energy gap of the two-level system.

AI.tldr: The study examines population transfer via chirped rapid adiabatic passage using open quantum and semiclassical models, with/without rotating-wave approximation, employing a time-dependent variational approach with multiple-Davydov D₂ trial state for quantum models. Robust population transfer is found over a wide parameter regime, insensitive to spin-phonon coupling, Gaussian pulse area, and energy gap.
AI.motivation: To examine the accuracy of semiclassical field description and the rotating-wave approximation in the context of chirped rapid adiabatic passage, and to identify the parameter regimes for robust population transfer.
AI.method: Open quantum and semiclassical models with/without rotating-wave approximation; time-dependent variational approach using the multiple-Davydov D₂ trial state to simulate quantum models with arbitrary finite mean photon number.
AI.result: Robust population transfer identified over a wide parameter regime controlled by laser spectral chirp; found to be insensitive to spin-phonon coupling strength, Gaussian pulse area, and energy gap of the two-level system.
AI.conclusion: Chirped rapid adiabatic passage enables robust population transfer across broad parameter conditions, with the semiclassical approximation and rotating-wave approximation validated under specific regimes.

title: Influence of laser chirp and interferometer delay and imbalance on the performance of a time-bin BB84 quantum key distribution system
summary: We investigate the effect of interferometer delay and imbalance on the performance of a BB84 time-bin quantum key distribution system. We simulate the impact of interference visibility on system performance and measure the visibility of a pair of interferometers as a function of their relative time delay and intensity imbalance. In addition, our analysis highlights the effect of laser chirp on system performance.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how interferometer delay and imbalance affect BB84 time-bin QKD performance, using simulations and measurements of visibility versus delay/imbalance, while also analyzing the impact of laser chirp.
AI.motivation: To understand how practical imperfections in interferometers (delay and imbalance) degrade the performance of time-bin BB84 QKD systems, and to examine the role of laser chirp in system performance.
AI.method: Simulation of the relationship between interference visibility and system performance, combined with experimental measurements of visibility as a function of relative time delay and intensity imbalance between a pair of interferometers.
AI.result: Quantified the dependence of interference visibility on interferometer delay and imbalance, and identified laser chirp as an additional degrading factor affecting system performance.
AI.conclusion: Interferometer imperfections (delay and imbalance) and laser chirp significantly impact BB84 time-bin QKD performance, and must be carefully controlled to maintain secure key distribution.

title: Heliciton-Assisted Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity from Helical Dirac Current
summary:
We develop a quantized chiral-field mechanism for chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). The corresponding quantum is a heliciton: a helical mode with phase coordinate $φ-qz$, screw momentum $\hbar q$, and energy $\hbarΩ_q$. A helical electron can absorb or emit this quantum, converting the static chiral vertex developed in our preceding work into an inelastic resonant scattering process. Using first Born scattering theory, we show that an incident two-spin-channel state generates two heliciton-assisted sidebands. Absorption converts the $\uparrow k$ channel into the $\downarrow,k+q$ sideband, while emission converts the $\downarrow k$ channel into the $\uparrow,k-q$ sideband. Thus the heliciton supplies both the screw momentum and energy needed to turn the handedness-conversion into a resonant spin-selective channel.
  The two sidebands inherit the same sampled-current overlap $J_χ(k)$ from the static theory, but acquire different kinematic weights and different resonance detunings. The sideband sector reaches full spin polarization at the respective isolated heliciton resonances, with $P_{\rm sb}(k,q)\simeq +1$ for $Δ_-(k,q)=0$ and $P_{\rm sb}(k,q)\simeq -1$ for $Δ_+(k,q)=0$. Reversing the screw handedness, $q\rightarrow -q$, interchanges the two sideband channels and reverses the polarization. No ad hoc spin-dependent potential is introduced. The spin selectivity comes from three ingredients: helical Dirac-current texture, quantized screw-symmetric environmental motion, and resonant exchange of screw momentum and energy. This identifies CISS as a heliciton-assisted resonance mechanism that produces spin polarization in the inelastic sideband sector.

AI.tldr: A quantized heliciton (helical quantum mode) mediates chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) by enabling inelastic resonant scattering that converts spin channels with opposite helicity, producing fully spin-polarized sidebands without ad hoc spin-dependent potentials.
AI.motivation: To develop a quantum-mechanical mechanism for CISS that goes beyond static chiral potentials by incorporating quantized environmental screw-symmetric motion as a dynamic, resonant process.
AI.method: Introduces a heliciton quantum (helical mode with phase coordinate φ−qz, screw momentum ℏq, energy ℏΩ_q). Uses first Born scattering theory to analyze two-spin-channel scattering with heliciton absorption/emission, producing sidebands with kinematic and detuning differences.
AI.result: The two sidebands exhibit full spin polarization (P_sb ≈ +1 or −1) at isolated heliciton resonances. Reversing screw handedness (q→−q) interchanges sideband channels and flips polarization. Spin selectivity arises from three ingredients: helical Dirac-current texture, quantized screw-symmetric motion, and resonant exchange of screw momentum/energy.
AI.conclusion: CISS is identified as a heliciton-assisted resonance mechanism producing spin polarization in the inelastic sideband sector, without invoking ad hoc spin-dependent potentials.

title: Far-field spatial coherence driven by lossy objects: first-principles approach unifying scattering of quantum light and thermal emission
summary: Far-field spatial coherence dictates the interference properties of scattered light and thermal emission. Traditionally, these phenomena are treated through disjointed paradigms: classical scattering descriptions assume cold objects lacking quantum fluctuations, idealized quantum scattering schemes ignore dissipation, and semiclassical fluctuational electrodynamics relies on phenomenological noise currents, precluding the consistent treatment of incident quantum states. Here, we develop a first-principles framework based on the modified Langevin noise formalism to unify the scattering of quantum light and the intrinsic thermal emission of finite dissipative objects. We demonstrate that the outgoing far-field spatial coherence separates into an algebraic superposition of two geometry-driven mechanisms, coupled by the global unitarity of the radiation-matter dynamics. The first mechanism, elastic scattering, acts as a non-unitary spatial filter, mode-selectively attenuating and reshaping incident quantum correlations. The second mechanism, thermal emission, originates from localized material dissipation and projects the object's absorption profile into the far field, providing a quantum-vectorial derivation of the macroscopic van Cittert-Zernike theorem. Applying this framework across optical regimes, we determine operational bounds for lossy quantum photonics. Under chaotic thermal illumination, we analytically demonstrate thermal cloaking at equilibrium and show that a passive sink casts a structured thermal shadow geometrically identical to a primary emitter. Under coherent illumination, we derive a thermodynamic phase diagram bounding macroscopic phase correlations, demonstrating that subwavelength nanostructures undergo substantial coherence degradation compared to bulk objects. Finally, under spatially entangled illumination...

AI.tldr: The paper develops a first-principles framework based on modified Langevin noise formalism that unifies quantum light scattering and thermal emission from finite dissipative objects, revealing that far-field spatial coherence separates into two geometry-driven mechanisms (elastic scattering and thermal emission) coupled by global unitarity.
AI.motivation: Existing paradigms for far-field spatial coherence are disjointed: classical scattering assumes cold objects without quantum fluctuations, idealized quantum scattering ignores dissipation, and fluctuational electrodynamics relies on phenomenological noise currents that cannot consistently treat incident quantum states.
AI.method: A first-principles modified Langevin noise formalism that unifies scattering of quantum light and intrinsic thermal emission of finite dissipative objects, incorporating quantum fluctuations and dissipation consistently.
AI.result: (1) Outgoing far-field coherence separates into elastic scattering (non-unitary spatial filter) and thermal emission (absorption profile projection). (2) Thermal cloaking at equilibrium demonstrated analytically. (3) Thermodynamic phase diagram bounding macroscopic phase correlations under coherent illumination showing subwavelength nanostructures undergo substantial coherence degradation. (4) Under spatially entangled illumination...
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a quantum-vectorial derivation of the macroscopic van Cittert-Zernike theorem and establishes operational bounds for lossy quantum photonics across different optical illumination regimes.

title: Overcoming the Speed-Fidelity Trade-off in Fast CZ Gates via Cyclic Control
summary: High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, at short durations, short-timescale waveform distortions break the time-reflection symmetry of control pulses, preventing the precise closure of cyclic evolution. This mechanism renders conventional symmetric protocols intrinsically over-constrained. Conventional strategies typically rely on smoothing the pulse envelopes or embedding the interaction pulse within a longer qubit pulse to bypass short-timescale distortions, which inevitably leads to a persistent speed-fidelity trade-off. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a cyclic control strategy based on parameter-space expansion, which restores controllability by incorporating an additional degree of freedom. We experimentally demonstrate this approach in a superconducting controlled-Z gate, achieving robust suppression of coherent errors without increasing gate duration, reducing the average coherent error from 0.27% to 0.12% across multiple two-qubit gates, as validated by cross-entropy benchmarking. Our results establish a general route to fast, high-fidelity cyclic quantum gates beyond the conventional speed-fidelity trade-off.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a cyclic control strategy based on parameter-space expansion that overcomes the speed-fidelity trade-off in quantum gates, demonstrated experimentally in a superconducting controlled-Z gate, reducing coherent errors from 0.27% to 0.12% without increasing gate duration.
AI.motivation: Short-timescale waveform distortions break the time-reflection symmetry of control pulses, preventing precise closure of cyclic evolution. Conventional symmetric protocols are over-constrained, and existing strategies (smoothing pulses or embedding within longer pulses) incur a speed-fidelity trade-off.
AI.method: A cyclic control strategy based on parameter-space expansion, which restores controllability by incorporating an additional degree of freedom, enabling robust suppression of coherent errors without increasing gate duration.
AI.result: Experimental demonstration in a superconducting controlled-Z gate: average coherent error reduced from 0.27% to 0.12% across multiple two-qubit gates, validated by cross-entropy benchmarking.
AI.conclusion: The results establish a general route to fast, high-fidelity cyclic quantum gates beyond the conventional speed-fidelity trade-off.

title: Leakage Mobility and Passive Leakage Removal in Transmons with Tunable Couplers
comment: Main text: 14 pages, 6 figures. Appendix: 6 pages, 1 figure
summary: Qubit leakage is a noticeable source of errors for quantum computing. In quantum processors, leakage excitations traveling between qubits generate correlated errors and perturb gate implementations. Leakage mobility can also be utilized for creating dedicated leakage removal pathways and removal units. To quantitatively characterize leakage mobility and to guide better design of processor architectures, we study here leakage dynamics in transmons with tunable couplers through numerical and analytical methods. Even if the couplers are tuned to cancel the single-excitation exchange or the ZZ interaction, the leakage hopping rates still persists in the range of 0.8-10 MHz due to transmon nonlinearity. In typical operation regimes, however, transmon frequency detuning localizes leakage excitations. The next-nearest-neighbor transmons can be still be near-resonant opening leakage tunneling channels. To suppress longer-range hopping, we find that the frequency spread of the next-nearest-neighbor transmons needs to be in the range of 1-4 MHz. Utilizing leakage mobility, we propose two passive leakage removal units. One is based on a tunable coupler and a pumped transmon, and another on a junction readout scheme. Based on realistic experimental parameters, our results on selectively mobilizing or localizing leakage excitations are readily applicable in superconducting quantum devices.

AI.tldr: This paper studies leakage dynamics in transmons with tunable couplers, finding leakage hopping persists at 0.8-10 MHz despite cancellation of exchange/ZZ interactions, and proposes two passive leakage removal units.
AI.motivation: Leakage excitations in quantum processors generate correlated errors, perturb gate implementations, and degrade quantum computing performance; understanding and controlling leakage mobility is essential for error mitigation and processor architecture design.
AI.method: Numerical and analytical analysis of leakage dynamics in transmons with tunable couplers; proposal of two passive leakage removal units (tunable coupler + pumped transmon, and junction readout scheme).
AI.result: Leakage hopping rates persist at 0.8-10 MHz due to transmon nonlinearity even when single-excitation exchange or ZZ interaction is canceled. Frequency detuning localizes leakage, but next-nearest-neighbor transmons can remain near-resonant. Frequency spread of 1-4 MHz is needed to suppress longer-range hopping.
AI.conclusion: The findings on selectively mobilizing or localizing leakage excitations are readily applicable to superconducting quantum devices for improved leakage management.

title: Quantum machine learning models for graphs
summary: Geometric Machine Learning (GML) successes have been achieved through the thorough study and design of new equivariant neural networks. In comparison, geometric quantum machine learning (GQML) models lack such a detailed understanding and, despite already several proposals, a unifying perspective on their design remains elusive. In this work, we focus on GQML models for graph problems that showcase a lot of structure and still remain frontier in machine learning. For the case when n-node graphs are encoded in n-qubit states, we provide a comprehensive characterization of their constituents. Taken together, these furnish us with a toolbox for the design of quantum graph models, and we further probe its benefits including the natural integration with classical models, generalization of known GQML models (sometimes extending their expressivity at virtually no cost), and straightforward classical pre-training strategies. The latter two features are demonstrated in dedicated numerical experiments.

AI.tldr: This work provides a comprehensive characterization and toolbox for designing geometric quantum machine learning (GQML) models for graph problems encoded in n-qubit states, offering benefits like integration with classical models, generalization of existing GQML models with extended expressivity, and classical pre-training strategies.
AI.motivation: While geometric machine learning (GML) has succeeded through well-studied equivariant neural networks, geometric quantum machine learning (GQML) models lack detailed understanding and a unifying design perspective, especially for structured graph problems.
AI.method: The authors provide a comprehensive characterization of GQML model constituents for n-node graphs encoded in n-qubit states, developing a toolbox for quantum graph model design.
AI.result: The proposed toolbox enables natural integration with classical models, generalization of known GQML models with extended expressivity at virtually no cost, and straightforward classical pre-training strategies—demonstrated through numerical experiments.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a unifying framework for GQML model design for graph problems, bridging the gap between classical GML successes and quantum ML approaches.

title: GsOQDC: A GUI-Driven Interactive Framework for End-to-End Simulation of Optical Quantum Data Centers
comment: Accepted for Demo in ECOC 2026, European Conference on Optical Communication
summary: We present GsOQDC, an open-source graphical framework integrating optical-network design, distributed quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and DES-based remote-gate simulation, enabling end-to-end cross-layer evaluation of entanglement-resource dynamics and system-level performance in Optical Quantum Data Centers.

AI.tldr: GsOQDC is an open-source graphical framework for end-to-end cross-layer evaluation of entanglement-resource dynamics and system-level performance in Optical Quantum Data Centers, integrating optical-network design, distributed quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and DES-based remote-gate simulation.
AI.motivation: To enable end-to-end cross-layer evaluation of entanglement-resource dynamics and system-level performance in Optical Quantum Data Centers, addressing the need for integrated tools that combine optical-network design, quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and simulation.
AI.method: The framework integrates optical-network design, distributed quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and discrete-event simulation (DES)-based remote-gate simulation.
